fw-01: Say thank you politely in Korean. Use 감사하다 + -(스)ㅂ니다.
fw-02: Introduce yourself in one sentence (your name or job). Use 저 + topic particle 은/는.
fw-03: Ask what an object near the listener is. Use the demonstrative (그 + 거) with 뭐 + -예요?
fw-04: State the price of an item using a Sino-Korean number, the currency unit 원, and -이에요.
fw-05: Politely order a drink (e.g. coffee) with a counter. Use 주다 + -(으)세요.
fw-06: Ask where a location (e.g. station or restroom) is. Use 어디 + -예요?
fw-07: Tell someone that you speak a little Korean. Use the adverb 조금 with 한국어 and 하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
fw-08: Place an order for drinks at a cafe with quantity. Use 주다 + -(으)세요.
gr-01: Write one routine activity you do every day (e.g. studying or exercising). Use a 하다 verb in the polite present (-아요/어요).
gr-02: Write one sentence about an activity you completed yesterday. Use the time word 어제 and past tense -았/었어요.
gr-03: Say what you are doing right now. Use an action verb + -고 있어요.
gr-04: Say one thing you choose not to do or eat. Use the short negative adverb 안 with a polite present verb.
gr-05: State what beverage you drink. Use 마시다 in the polite present with object particle 을/를.
gr-06: Say where you study or work. Use a location noun with action location particle 에서 and a polite present verb.
gr-07: Compare two things or times (e.g. today and yesterday). Use the comparison particle 보다.
gr-08: Connect two contrasting statements into one sentence. Use an adjective or verb stem + -지만.
bg-04-01: State that you were the one who ordered the food. Use 저 + -가 (subject focus) and 주문하다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-04-02: Contrast one drink or food you like with one you do not. Use topic particle 은/는 for contrast and 좋아하다 + -지만.
bg-05-01: State that you are a student. Use 학생 + identification copula -이에요/예요.
bg-05-02: State that you are not a singer. Use 가수 + -이/가 and 아니다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-05-03: Point to an item and state that it is a desk. Use 이거는 with 책상 + -이에요/예요.
bg-05-04: Clarify that you are a student, not a teacher. Use 선생님 + -이/가 with 아니다 (-아요/어요), and 학생 + -이에요/예요.
bg-06-01: State that you have time today. Use 시간 + -이/가 and 있다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-06-02: State that you eat a meal at a restaurant. Use 식당 + -에서 and 먹다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-06-03: Suggest meeting someone at three o'clock. Use the native Korean number for three + 시 + time particle -에, and 만나다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-06-04: State what object is in your room or bag. Use a location with static location particle -에 and 있다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-07-01: State that you cook at home. Use 집 + action location particle -에서 and 요리하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-07-02: Suggest having lunch together with a friend. Use adverb 같이 with 점심 and 먹다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-07-03: Suggest taking a walk in the park together. Use 공원 + -에서 and 산책하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-07-04: A friend asks what you do this evening. Reply that you rest at home. Use 집 + -에서 and 쉬다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-08-01: State what you read every day. Use 책 + object particle -을/를 and 읽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-08-02: State that you like coffee (with contrast). Use 커피 + topic particle -은/는 for contrast and 좋아하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-08-03: Write a sentence stating that you learn Korean. Use 저 + topic particle -은/는, 한국어 + object particle -을/를, and 배우다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-08-04: State that you are eating pizza. Use 피자 + object particle -을/를 and 먹다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-09-01: State that you do not work on weekends. Use noun 일 with short negation 안 and 하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-09-02: State that you cannot swim due to inability. Use noun 수영 with negative adverb 못 and 하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-09-03: Explain that you cannot drink alcohol because you are driving. Use 운전하다 + -아/어서 with negative adverb 못 and 마시다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-09-04: State that this food is not expensive. Use short negation 안 with adjective 비싸다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-10-01: State where you went yesterday (e.g. library). Use time word 어제 and 가다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-10-02: State that you drank coffee a little while ago. Use time adverb 아까 and 마시다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-10-03: State that you wrote a diary entry in Korean. Use 한국어 + language particle -(으)로 and 쓰다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-10-04: State that you listened to music yesterday. Use time word 어제 and 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-11-01: Say what you are doing at the library right now. Use 도서관 + -에서 and 공부하다 + -고 있어요.
bg-11-02: State that you are resting at home right now. Use 집 + -에서 and 쉬다 + -고 있어요.
bg-11-03: State that you are wearing a hat. Use 모자 + object particle -을/를 and wear verb 쓰다 + -고 있어요.
bg-11-04: Reply to a friend that you are waiting for the bus. Use 버스 + object particle -을/를 and 기다리다 + -고 있어요.
bg-12-01: State that you wash your hands before eating a meal. Use 먹다 + -기 전에 and 손을 씻다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-12-02: State what you do when you are tired. Use 피곤하다 + -(으)ㄹ 때 and 쉬다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-12-03: State that it has been 3 months since you started learning Korean. Use 배우다 + -(으)ㄴ 지 and 되다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-12-04: State that you read a book before going to sleep. Use 자다 + -기 전에 and 책을 읽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-01: Connect two sequential actions: eating a meal and drinking coffee. Use 먹다 + -고 and 마시다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-13-02: Contrast the price and taste of a dish (expensive but delicious). Use 비싸다 + -지만 and 맛있다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-03: Connect listening to music and reading a newspaper in the morning. Use 듣다 + -고 and 읽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-13-04: Contrast someone being busy with always being kind. Use 바쁘다 + -지만 and 친절하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-14-01: Write one sentence saying you rested at home because you were tired. Use 피곤하다 + -아/어서 and 쉬다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-14-02: Suggest going inside because it is cold outside. Use 춥다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)니까 and 들어가다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-14-03: Tell someone to close the window because it is cold outside. Use 춥다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)니까 and 닫다 + -(으)세요.
bg-14-04: Politely apologize for being late to an appointment. Use 늦다 + -아/어서 and 죄송하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-15-01: State what improves if you read a lot of books. Use 읽다 + -(으)면 and 좋아지다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-15-02: State that you greet a friend while smiling. Use 웃다 + -(으)면서 and 인사하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-15-03: State that you drink coffee or tea in the morning. Use 마시다 + -거나 to connect the alternatives.
bg-15-04: State two alternate activities you do if you have free time. Use 있다 + -(으)면 and 읽다 + -거나.
bg-16-01: Set the background that you are going to the bookstore now. Use 서점 + direction particle -에 and 가다 + -는데.
bg-16-02: Suggest going for a walk because the weather is nice. Use 좋다 + -(으)ㄴ데 and 산책하다 + -(으)ㄹ까요?
bg-16-03: Politely decline an invitation by saying you want to go but are busy today. Use -고 싶다 + -(으)ㄴ데 and 바쁘다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-16-04: Politely preface a question by saying you have a question. Use 질문 + -이/가 and 있다 + -는데.
bg-17-01: Tell someone to read a book slowly. Use adverb 천천히 and 읽다 + -(으)세요.
bg-17-02: Politely ask someone to speak slowly for you. Use adverb 천천히 and 말하다 + -아/어 주세요.
bg-17-03: Ask someone to listen to your story as a favor. Use 이야기 + object particle -을/를 and 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) + -아/어 주세요.
bg-17-04: Ask someone to close the door for you because it is noisy outside. Use 닫다 + -아/어 주세요.
bg-18-01: Ask for permission to eat an apple. Use 사과 + object particle -을/를 and 먹다 + -아/어도 돼요?
bg-18-02: State that you must clean your room today. Use 방 + object particle -을/를 and 청소하다 + -아/어야 돼요.
bg-18-03: State that you may go home now because work or class is finished. Use 집 + -에 and 가다 + -아/어도 돼요.
bg-18-04: Ask if you may charge your phone here. Use 휴대폰 + object particle -을/를 and 충전하다 + -아/어도 돼요?
bg-19-01: Politely tell someone not to eat late at night. Use the time expression 밤에 and 먹다 + -지 마세요.
bg-19-02: Politely warn someone not to touch a picture with their hands. Use 손 + -(으)로 (by means of) and 만지다 + -지 마세요.
bg-19-03: State a rule that you must not park here. Use 여기 + -에 and 주차하다 + -(으)면 안 돼요.
bg-19-04: Comfort a nervous friend before an exam. Use the adverb 너무 and 긴장하다 + -지 마세요.
bg-20-01: State that you can swim. Use 수영 and 하다 + -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요.
bg-20-02: Explain that you cannot meet today because you are busy. Use 바쁘다 + -아/어서 and 만나다 + -(으)ㄹ 수 없어요.
bg-20-03: State that you can listen to Korean songs. Use 한국 노래 with 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) + -(으)ㄹ 수 있어요.
bg-20-04: State that you cannot drive due to lack of skill. Use 운전 + object particle -을/를 and 못하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-21-01: Suggest drinking coffee together. Use adverb 같이 and 마시다 + -(으)ㄹ까요?
bg-21-02: Promise to call someone tomorrow. Use time word 내일 and 전화하다 + -(으)ㄹ게요.
bg-21-03: Express your personal intention to rest at home today. Use 집 + -에서 and 쉬다 + -(으)ㄹ래요.
bg-21-04: Volunteer to buy dinner for your friend. Use 저 + -가 (subject focus) and 사다 + -(으)ㄹ게요.
bg-22-01: Ask a friend if they have tried eating kimchi. Use 김치 and 먹다 + -아/어 봤어요?
bg-22-02: State that you have never been skiing (riding skis). Use 스키 with 타다 + -(으)ㄴ 적이 없어요.
bg-22-03: State that you have watched Korean dramas before. Use 한국 드라마 with 보다 + -(으)ㄴ 적이 있어요.
bg-22-04: Recommend visiting Jeju Island to a friend. Use 제주도 + direction particle -에 and 가다 + -아/어 보세요.
bg-23-01: State that you go to the library to study. Use 공부하다 + -(으)러 and 가다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-23-02: State that you intend to buy a computer. Use 컴퓨터 and 사다 + -(으)려고 해요.
bg-23-03: State that you decided to meet someone at 2 o'clock. Use 2시 + time particle -에 and 만나다 + -기로 했어요.
bg-23-04: State that you decided to go to Korea. Use 한국 + direction particle -에 and 가다 + -기로 했어요.
bg-24-01: Express your softened impression that the weather seems hot today. Use 날씨 + -이/가 and adjective 덥다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요.
bg-24-02: Predict that tomorrow's weather will be good. Use time word 내일 and 좋다 + -(으)ㄹ 것 같아요.
bg-24-03: State that you think your friend has already arrived. Use 친구 + -이/가 and 오다 + -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요.
bg-24-04: Softly say you feel the size is a bit small. Use 사이즈 + -이/가 and 작다 + -(으)ㄴ 것 같아요.
bg-25-01: Give gentle advice that it is good to drink warm water. Use 따뜻한 물 and 마시다 + -는 게 좋아요.
bg-25-02: Express your wish that school vacation comes soon. Use 방학 + -이/가 and 오다 + -았/었으면 좋겠어요.
bg-25-03: Express a wish to hear good news tomorrow. Use 좋은 소식 + object particle -을/를 and 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) + -았/었으면 좋겠어요.
bg-25-04: Give caring advice to go to sleep early when tired. Use adverb 일찍 and 자다 + -는 게 좋아요.
bg-26-01: Express that you have come to like Korean food. Use 한국 음식 + object particle -을/를 and 좋아하다 + -게 되다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-26-02: Wish someone an enjoyable meal for lunch. Use 점심, adverbial form 맛있다 + -게, and honorific 드시다 + -(으)세요.
bg-26-03: Politely ask someone to explain the grammar easily. Use 문법 + -을/를, adverbial form 쉽다 (ㅂ irregular) + -게, and 설명하다 + -아/어 주세요.
bg-26-04: Express a personal resolution to exercise every day for your health. Use 매일 운동 and 하다 + -기로 했어요.
bg-27-01: State that this is the song you are listening to right now. Use 지금 with 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) + present modifier -는, and 노래 + -예요.
bg-27-02: Suggest having coffee together when there is free time. Use 시간 + -이/가 with 있다 + -(으)ㄹ 때, and 커피 마시다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-27-03: Describe the book you read yesterday and say it was very moving. Use the time word 어제, 읽다 + past modifier -(으)ㄴ before 책, and 정말 감동적이다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-27-04: Say that you already reserved a movie you plan to watch on the weekend. Use 주말 + -에, 보다 + future modifier -(으)ㄹ before 영화, and 미리 예약하다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-28-01: Formally announce that you will start the presentation. Use 지금 발표 and 시작하다 + -겠습니다.
bg-28-02: Formally instruct passengers to step back. Use 뒤로 and 물러서다 + -아/어 주십시오.
bg-28-03: State formally that you make Korean food. Use 한국 요리 and 만들다 (ㄹ irregular) in the formal polite style (-ㅂ니다/습니다).
bg-28-04: Close a formal job interview with a polite request for goodwill. Use 앞으로 and 잘 부탁드리다 in the formal polite style (-ㅂ니다/습니다).
bg-29-01: Honorifically describe the teacher reading a book in the classroom. Use 선생님 and 책을 읽다 with honorific -(으)시- in the polite present (-세요).
bg-29-02: Honorifically state that your grandmother is coming home today. Use 할머니 + honorific subject particle -께서 and 집에 오다 with honorific -(으)시- (-세요).
bg-29-03: Describe your mother calling your grandmother. Use 어머니 + -께서, 할머니 + honorific dative particle -께, and 전화를 하다 with honorific -(으)시- (-세요).
bg-29-04: Describe accompanying your grandmother to the hospital on the weekend. Use 할머니 + object particle -를 with humble verb 모시다 + -고, and 병원에 가다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-30-01: Compliment someone's Korean speaking ability with spontaneous exclamation. Use 한국어 + object particle -를 with 정말 잘하시다 + -네요!
bg-30-02: Express realization that someone has lived in Korea for a long time. Use 한국에서 오래 with honorific 사시다 + past realization -었군요.
bg-30-03: Confirm the meeting time tomorrow by seeking agreement. Use 내일 회의 with time 2시 + confirmation ending -지요?
bg-30-04: Chime in with spontaneous praise for homemade food. Use 직접 만들다 (ㄹ irregular) + -(으)ㄴ before 음식, and 정말 맛있다 + -네요!
bg-31-01: State that you gave a gift to your younger sibling. Use 동생 + recipient particle -한테, 선물 + object particle -을/를, and 주다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-31-02: State that you received a phone call from a friend. Use 친구 + source particle -한테서, 전화 + object particle -을/를, and 받다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-31-03: Give directions telling someone to go to the right at the traffic light. Use 오른쪽 + direction particle -(으)로 and 가다 + -(으)세요.
bg-31-04: State that you go to the station by subway. Use 지하철 + transport particle -(으)로 and 가다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-32-01: Compare today and yesterday's weather. Use 어제 + comparison particle -보다 and 따뜻하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-32-02: State that lunch time is from 12 to 1 o'clock. Use starting time 12시 + -부터 and ending time 1시 + -까지 with copula -이에요/예요.
bg-32-03: State that you only drank water this morning. Use 물 + exclusive particle -만 and 마시다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-32-04: State that someone sings like a professional singer. Use 가수 + comparison particle -처럼 and 노래하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-33-01: State that you watched a movie with a friend over the weekend. Use 친구 + connective particle -(이)랑, 영화 + object particle -을/를, and 보다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-33-02: Offer a choice to drink either cold water or juice. Use 물 + alternative particle -(이)나 and 주스 + object particle -을/를 with 드시다 + -(으)세요.
bg-33-03: State that you also study Korean diligently. Use 저 + additive particle -도, 한국어 + object particle -을/를, and 공부하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-33-04: State that you also like Korean food very much. Use 저 + additive particle -도, 한국 음식 + object particle -을/를, and 좋아하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-34-01: State that your hobby is watching movies. Use 취미 + topic particle -은/는, and 영화 보다 nominalized with -기 + copula -예요.
bg-34-02: State that you received great help from a friend when times were difficult. Use 친구 + source particle -한테서, noun 도움 + object particle -을/를, and 받다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
bg-34-03: State that you study listening and speaking for the Korean exam. Use 듣다 nominalized with -기 + connective -와, and 말하다 with -기 + object particle -를.
bg-34-04: State that a book is easy to read because its content is simple. Use verb 읽다 + nominalizer -기 and 쉽다 (ㅂ irregular) in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-35-01: Ask how many apples are in the basket. Use 사과 + subject particle -이/가, question phrase 몇 개, and 있다 in the polite present question (-어요?).
bg-35-02: State that two students are studying in the classroom. Use noun phrase 학생 두 명 + subject particle -이/가 and 공부하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-35-03: Order two cups of warm coffee at a cafe. Use noun phrase 커피 두 잔 and 주다 + -(으)세요.
bg-35-04: State that you are twenty years old this year. Use 올해 and the native Korean number for twenty + 살 + -이에요/예요.
bg-36-01: Ask what something is called in Korean. Use 이거 and 뭐 + -예요?
bg-36-02: Ask when your friend's birthday is. Use 생일 + -이/가 and 언제 + -예요?
bg-36-03: Ask a friend which country they came from. Use question phrase 어느 나라 + source particle -에서 and 오다 in the past tense (-았/었어요?).
bg-36-04: Ask someone what kind of Korean food they like most. Use question phrase 무슨 음식 + object particle -을/를 and 좋아하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요?).
bg-d-01-01: A friend asks where you go after class. Reply that you go to the cinema. Use 극장 + direction particle -에 and 가다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-d-01-02: A friend asks what you do at the library. Reply that you read books. Use 책 + object particle -을/를 and 읽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-d-01-03: A friend asks what you do in the morning. Reply that you drink coffee. Use 커피 + object particle -을/를 and 마시다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-d-01-04: A friend asks where you rest on weekends. Reply that you rest at home. Use 집 + action location particle -에서 and 쉬다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-d-02-01: A friend asks what you want to do on vacation. Express your desire to visit Jeju Island. Use 제주도 + direction particle -에 and 가다 + -고 싶어요.
bg-d-02-02: A friend asks what you will do tomorrow. Reply with your plan to go to the library. Use 도서관 + direction particle -에 and 가다 + -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
bg-d-02-03: Express a future wish to travel to Europe someday. Use adverb 언젠가 with destination 유럽 and 가다 + -고 싶어요.
bg-d-02-04: A friend asks about your dinner plans. Reply that you will bake a cake. Use 케이크 + object particle -을/를 and 만들다 (ㄹ irregular) + -(으)ㄹ 거예요.
bg-d-03-01: A friend asks where the teacher is going. Reply honorifically that the teacher goes to the classroom. Use 선생님 and 가다 with honorific -(으)시- (-세요).
bg-d-03-02: A colleague asks if the teacher is in the office. Reply that the teacher is present. Use 선생님 and honorific existence verb 계시다 in the polite present (-어요).
bg-d-03-03: Ask a senior politely where their home is. Use honorific noun 댁 + -이/가 and question word 어디 with honorific copula -(이)세요?
bg-d-03-04: Politely ask the teacher where they live. Use question word 어디 and honorific form of 살다 (사시다, ㄹ drops) in the polite question (-세요?).
bg-d-04-01: State that the teacher went to the hospital yesterday. Use 선생님 + honorific subject particle -께서, adverb 어제, and honorific past form of 가다 (가시다 + -았/었어요).
bg-d-04-02: State formally that the department head arrives shortly. Use 부장님 + honorific subject particle -께서, adverb 곧, and verb 도착하다 in the formal honorific present (-(으)십니다).
bg-d-04-03: Politely offer warm tea to a customer. Use noun phrase 따뜻한 차 and honorific verb 드시다 with polite question suffix -겠어요?
bg-d-04-04: Ask a colleague if the director is in the office right now. Use 사장님 + honorific subject particle -께서, location 사무실 + -에, and honorific existence verb 계시다 in the polite question form (-어요?).
bg-d-05-01: Write a formal polite instruction telling a customer to wait a moment. Use adverb 잠시만 and verb 기다리다 + formal imperative -(으)십시오.
bg-d-05-02: Propose starting the meeting together in a formal gathering. Use 회의 + object particle -를, adverb phrase 다 같이, and verb 시작하다 + formal propositive -(으)십시다.
bg-d-05-03: Humbly state that you will ask the teacher. Use 선생님 + honorific particle -께 and humble verb 여쭙다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)ㄹ게요.
bg-d-05-04: Humbly offer to carry luggage for grandmother. Use 짐 + object particle -을 and compound verb 들다 with humble helper 드리다 + -(으)ㄹ게요.
bg-irr-01-01: State that your head hurts today. Use 머리 + subject particle -가 and ㅡ irregular adjective 아프다 in the polite present (-아요).
bg-irr-01-02: State that Korean is really easy. Use 한국어 + subject particle -가, adverb 정말, and ㅂ irregular adjective 쉽다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-irr-01-03: State that you walk in the park every day. Use 공원 + object particle -을, adverb 매일, and ㄷ irregular verb 걷다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-irr-01-04: State that you wear warm clothes. Use modifier 따뜻한 with 옷 + object particle -을, and regular verb 입다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-irr-02-01: State that you listen to music every day. Use 저 + topic particle -는, adverb 매일, 음악 + object particle -을, and ㄷ irregular verb 듣다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-irr-02-02: State that you do not know the answer. Use 저 + topic particle -는, 답 + object particle -을, and 르 irregular verb 모르다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-irr-02-03: State that you press the elevator button. Use compound noun 엘리베이터 버튼 + object particle -을 and 르 irregular verb 누르다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
bg-irr-02-04: State that two people's personalities are different from each other. Use phrase 두 사람 + topic particle -은, 성격 + subject particle -이, adverb 서로, and 르 irregular adjective 다르다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
im-02-02-01: Apologize for not answering the phone because you were driving. Use 운전하다 + -느라고 and 전화 + 못 받다 in the polite past tense (-았/었어요).
im-02-02-02: State that you stayed up all night making cards to give to a friend. Use 카드 + object particle -를, 만들다 (ㄹ irregular) + -느라고, and 밤을 새우다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
im-02-02-03: State that you could not hear the doorbell because you were listening to music with earphones. Use 음악 + 듣다 (ㄷ irregular) + -느라고 and 벨 소리 + object particle -를 with 못 듣다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
im-02-02-04: Write a professional email apology explaining that your reply was delayed due to reviewing the proposal. Use 제안서 + object particle -를, verb 검토하다 + -느라고, and verb 늦다 in the formal past tense (-았습니다/었습니다).
im-02-03-01: State that you were late for school because the bus did not come. Use 버스 + subject particle -가, 안 오다 + -는 바람에, and 늦다 in the polite past tense (-았/었어요).
im-02-03-02: Explain that the video conference connection was cut off because the internet disconnected. Use 인터넷 + 끊어지다 + -는 바람에 and 연결 + 끊기다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
im-02-03-03: State that you walked to work during rush hour because you could not catch a taxi. Use 택시 + 안 잡히다 + -는 바람에 and compound motion verb 걸어서 가다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
im-02-03-04: State that you almost bumped into someone because the person in front stopped abruptly. Use 앞사람 + 갑자기 서다 + -는 바람에 and verb 부딪치다 + -(으)ㄹ 뻔하다 in the past tense (-았/었어요).
im-03-01-01: Observe people holding umbrellas and infer that it is raining outside. Use 우산 + 쓰다 + -(으)ㄴ 걸 보니 and 비 + 오다 + -나 보다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
im-03-01-02: Observe people wearing clothes thickly and guess that the weather is cold. Use 옷 + adverb 두껍게 with 입다 + -(으)ㄴ 걸 보니 and 춥다 (ㅂ irregular) + -(으)ㄴ가 보다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
im-03-01-03: React empathetically upon hearing that someone won first place. Use 소식 + object particle -을, ㄷ irregular verb 듣다 + -(으)니, adverb 정말, and 기쁘다 + exclamatory conjectural ending -겠군요.
im-03-01-04: Comfort a colleague who worked overtime late into the night. Use phrase 늦게까지 일하다 + -느라 and honorific phrase 고생 많으시다 with conjectural exclamatory ending -었겠군요.
im-03-02-01: Express astonishment that this year has already reached its final month. Use phrase 벌써 올해 마지막 달 + exclamation particle -(이)라니 and verb 믿기지 않다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
im-03-02-02: Express sadness upon hearing that a colleague is leaving the company. Use 회사 + object particle -를, 그만두다 + quotation reaction suffix -(느)ㄴ다니, and 섭섭하다 in the polite present (-아요/어요).
im-03-02-03: Acknowledge with realization that an important meeting has been postponed to next week. Use 회의 + subject particle -가, 다음 주 + direction particle -(으)로, and passive verb 연기되다 + realization ending -었군요.
im-03-02-04: Remind a close friend of plans to meet for dinner tonight. Use time phrase 오늘 저녁, verb 만나다 + -기로 하다, and verb 약속하다 with intimate reminder ending -았/었잖아.
